title: Penelope's Web
beat: Antinous rejects Telemachus's charge and blames Penelope for prolonging the courtship.
text: 'It is not the suitors who are to blame, it is your own mother, for she is the most artful woman in the world. This three years past, and close on four, she has been driving us out of our minds.'
guess: Telemachus confronting the suitors in the hall (or a suitor taking the young man's spear as he arrives in the palace).
sees: Bright colonnaded hall with white columns, cream walls with red trim, a gold throne/table. In foreground a blonde man in blue coat from behind holding a long spear. Facing him are several men with long hair and moustaches (purple, green-patterned, green shirt), one grasping the spear point, one waving.
why: The spear tip appears to pass into the man's hand; foreground figure's face hidden; tone of the encounter (hostile vs welcoming) unclear.

title: Penelope's Web
beat: He recounts how she wove Laertes's shroud by day and secretly unraveled it by night.
text: 'She set up a great tambour frame in her room, and began to work on an enormous piece of fine needlework. "Sweethearts," said she, "wait till I have completed a pall for the hero Laertes."'
guess: Penelope at her loom, weaving (and unweaving) Laertes' shroud to put off the suitors.
sees: Sunny LEGO courtyard with white columns, tan walls with red trim, tables. A tall wooden frame with vertical threads/rods and white cloth (a loom). A woman with hair in a bun wearing pink stands next to it, smiling and gesturing.
why: Loom could be read as a cage or door; woman is floating slightly and just gestures rather than weaving; no suitors clearly visible.

title: Penelope's Web
beat: By night she unravelled what she had woven by day.
text: 'This was how she deceived us. She used to keep working at it all day long, but at night she would unpick the stitches again by torchlight.'
guess: Penelope at her loom weaving (and secretly unweaving) Laertes' shroud to delay the suitors.
sees: Dim hall with stone columns and a dark ceiling. A tall wooden upright loom with woven cloth and hanging weights/threads. A woman in red and white with brown hair stands beside it, one hand on the frame. Quiet, night-time mood.
why: She appears to float slightly off the floor; nothing indicates weaving vs. unweaving.

title: Penelope's Web
beat: A maid exposed the deception and the suitors forced Penelope to finish the web.
text: 'But in the fourth year one of her maids who knew what she was doing told us, and we caught her in the act of undoing her work, so she had to finish it whether she would or no.'
guess: Penelope at her loom confronting or putting off the suitors in the hall of Ithaca.
sees: Dark hall with a white column, tan walls, red trim, a loom-like structure with vertical rods at left. A woman in red/maroon with a brown bun stands elevated on the left, gesturing. An old grey-haired woman in white, and several men (green coat, purple coat with moustache, long hair) face her; one is drinking from a large translucent amber cup that passes through his head.
why: The huge transparent amber cup clips through a man's head and is oddly scaled; the woman appears to float above the floor; dark lighting.

title: Penelope's Web
beat: Antinous demands that Telemachus send his mother back to Icarius to choose a husband.
text: 'Send your mother away, and bid her marry the man of her own and of her father's choice... as long as she persists in tormenting us, we will go on eating up your estate.'
guess: Telemachus confronting the suitors in Odysseus' hall (with Penelope's loom behind).
sees: Sunny courtyard with white columns and a tall wooden frame (loom or doorway). A young man in blue holds a long spear diagonally; a woman in pink raises a cup behind; men in green and red tunics stand around; an older woman at right.
why: Foreground figures block the view; unclear if the frame is a loom; no clear action.

title: The Wooden Horse
beat: Menelaus answers with the story of the wooden horse.
text: 'What endurance too, and what courage he displayed within the wooden horse, wherein all the bravest of the Argives were lying in wait to bring death and destruction upon the Trojans.'
guess: The Trojan Horse standing inside or outside the walls of Troy at night.
sees: A night scene on a small tan baseplate against dark space. A large tan brick horse on legs with dark red mane pieces stands beside a crenellated city wall and tower. There are torches and red and tan blocks, maybe carts or crates, and a checkered floor under the horse.
why: The horse is blocky and abstract. There are no figures to show the action.

title: The Wooden Horse
beat: Helen circled the horse and imitated the voices of the warriors' wives.
text: 'Three times did you go all round our hiding place and pat it with your hands, calling our chiefs each by his own name, and mimicking all our wives.'
guess: At the Trojan Horse in Troy at night. Perhaps Cassandra warning the Trojans, or Helen calling to the Greeks hidden inside.
sees: Night, low angle. A woman in a blue top with a gold headpiece raises both hands. She stands under the belly of a huge tan block horse with dark red mane pieces. City walls and a tower with a red cap are behind her, a torch is in the foreground, and there are dark red blocks.
why: The horse is so huge and close that it reads as a building. It is ambiguous whether her raised hands mean alarm or celebration.

title: The Wooden Horse
beat: The hidden Greeks nearly answered; Odysseus restrained them and silenced Anticlus.
text: 'Diomed, myself, and the son of Tydeus who were inside heard what a noise you made, and would have gone out; but Ulysses held us back... Anticlus alone would have answered you, but Ulysses kept his hands pressed firmly over his mouth.'
guess: Possibly Helen appearing before the Trojan elders/warriors at the walls of Troy (or a woman slipping past guards at a city gate)
sees: Night scene; tan stone tower/gatehouse with an upper gallery holding four figures, three in crested helmets (red/orange tunics, one in white robe); below in the gateway a smiling woman in blue top waving; dark sky, warm interior light.
why: Relationship between upper group and woman unclear; one helmeted figure's face hidden; nighttime darkness; small object floating top right.

title: The Wooden Horse
beat: Telemachus hears proof of his father's endurance and command under pressure.
text: 'He kept his hands pressed firmly over his mouth till Minerva took you away again.'
guess: Greek warriors hiding inside the Trojan Horse (Odysseus keeping the men quiet).
sees: Cramped dark wooden interior; four soldiers in crested Greek helmets, one bearded man in red without helmet holding his hands up near his face as if gesturing silence or peering; they stand on a wooden platform above an opening.
why: Scale and space are confusing; hard to tell it is a horse from inside; the gesture could be covering eyes or hushing.

title: Menelaus and Proteus
beat: Telemachus asks directly for news of Odysseus.
text: 'Tell me, then, about my father... whether he is alive or dead, and whether you saw him with your own eyes.'
guess: Proteus, the Old Man of the Sea, among his seals on Pharos before Menelaus seizes him.
sees: Rocky grey crag with a cave by the shore. An old crowned king with white beard in a red coat holds a staff. Three grey seals lie at the water's edge in front of him. Bright daylight.
why: Nothing distinguishes the seals' role; no other characters present to fix the moment.

title: Menelaus and Proteus
beat: Menelaus recounts being trapped in Egypt until Eidothea taught him to seize Proteus.
text: 'A goddess, Idothea, daughter of Proteus the old man of the sea, took pity on me... "Lie in wait for him and catch him; he will tell you about your voyage."'
guess: Proteus, the Old Man of the Sea, with his seals and his daughter Eidothea (from Menelaus' tale in the Odyssey).
sees: Shoreline with green grass, sand and blue sea. A long-haired woman in purple stands at the water's edge with a hand raised. A crowned white-bearded old man in red holding a staff stands at right. Seals lie on the shore at both sides. Calm sky.
why: The old man's back is turned so his relation to the woman is unclear; the seals are cut off at the edges.

title: Menelaus and Proteus
beat: He and three men hid beneath sealskins and grappled the Old Man of the Sea.
text: 'She had brought four seal skins from the bottom of the sea... she dug four pits for us to lie in, and made us lie down in them, and threw a sealskin over each of us. The stench of the fishy seals was most distressing.'
guess: Poseidon's wrath: the Phaeacian ship turned to stone, with King Alcinous bowing/submitting in fear (or Poseidon punishing).
sees: Beach with sand and grass, grey boat-shaped rocks scattered on shore, grey cliff at right. In foreground a crowned bearded man in red is bent over/crawling, only head and hands visible; behind him a white-bearded crowned figure with a trident-like object stands.
why: Foreground king oddly posed, body hidden behind a rock; stone shapes ambiguous (boats or rocks); the relation between figures is unclear.

title: Menelaus and Proteus
beat: Proteus changed into beasts, water, and a tree before yielding prophecy.
text: 'He began by turning into a lion with a great mane; then all of a sudden he became a dragon, a leopard, a wild boar; the next moment he was running water, and then again directly he was a tree; but we stuck to him and never lost hold.'
guess: Menelaus and his companions holding Proteus as he shape-shifts into lion, serpent, water and tree (Odyssey IV)
sees: Grassy island by the sea; a large yellow lion, a green snake, a white column-like tree with smoke/water droplets, a real tree; an old bearded crowned man in red arms raised in the middle; two curly-haired men grabbing at him from either side; grey rock and a grey seal-like creature at left.
why: Lion blocks the central figure; the white spouting column is odd; many elements overlap.

title: Menelaus and Proteus
beat: He revealed that Odysseus lived, detained by Calypso on an island.
text: 'I saw him in an island sorrowing bitterly in the house of the nymph Calypso, who is keeping him prisoner, and he cannot reach his home.'
guess: Menelaus and his men ambushing Proteus, the Old Man of the Sea, among his seals to force a prophecy.
sees: LEGO shoreline at dusk: green grass, sand, blue sea. White-bearded crowned figure in white robes, another crowned figure in red, curly-haired figures, white-haired figure by grey rocks; grey seal-like creatures lying on the shore.
why: Seals are ambiguous shapes; two crowned figures confuse who is who; no clear grappling.

title: Calypso's Raft
beat: Calypso leads Odysseus to tall trees and gives him axe, adze, augers, cloth, and cord.
text: She gave him a great bronze axe that suited his hands... Then she led the way to the far end of the island where the largest trees grew: alder, poplar and pine, that reached the sky.
guess: Possibly Odysseus meeting a woman/goddess on an island (Nausicaa, Circe or Calypso) or being led by a guide.
sees: Sunny LEGO landscape with trees, purple flowers, a tan cliff on the right, water behind. A blonde long-haired figure in a teal top seen from behind, and a brown-haired man in a pink shirt holding a cup, also from behind.
why: Both figures are seen from behind so faces and interaction are unreadable; the blonde figure is partly behind a tree; no clear action or props.

title: Calypso's Raft
beat: He fells, trims, bores, joins, decks, and fences the timbers over four days.
text: Twenty trees in all did he cut down, and then trimmed them with the axe; he smoothed them with his adze and made them straight by the line.
guess: Odysseus on Calypso's island (Ogygia), either weeping by the shore longing for home or cutting timber for his raft.
sees: Brick-built landscape: tall green conifers, purple flowers, tan rocky cliff, sea behind. A blond minifigure in pink top and white legs sits on or among fallen brown logs, one hand raised to his head. Bright daylight, calm but lonely mood.
why: Figure partly hidden behind a tree; the gesture is ambiguous (waving, weeping, thinking); the grey shape behind him is hard to identify; logs could be a raft or just fallen trees.

title: Calypso's Raft
beat: He rigs mast, yard, sail, steering oar, and ballast.
text: He also made a mast with a yard arm, and a rudder to steer with... Calypso brought him some linen to make the sails, and he made these too, excellently.
guess: Odysseus leaving Calypso's island on the raft he built, Calypso giving him provisions (Odyssey Book 5).
sees: Bright island scene: tan rocky cliffs with a dark cave mouth, green grass with purple flowers and tall conifers, blue sea. A small brown raft with a mast and blank white sail sits at the shore. A blonde woman holding a jug/cup stands by the cave; a bearded man in red holds a sword aloft and a bow. A stray oar/log in the water.
why: The sail is a flat white brick wall; the man seems to hold both a sword and a bow at once; hard to tell if he is on the raft or on shore; the floating log's purpose is unclear.

title: Calypso's Raft
beat: Calypso bathes and clothes him, loads food and water, and sends a warm wind behind the raft.
text: She sent him a warm and gentle wind to blow him along, and glad indeed was Ulysses as he spread his sail before it.
guess: Odysseus leaving Calypso's island on the raft he built, with Calypso waving farewell from her cave.
sees: A man in red holds a sword up and has a bow in front of him. He stands on a small brown raft with a mast and a big white sail on blue water. Behind him is a sandy rock cliff with a dark cave. A blonde woman in pale blue stands on the shore waving a white cloth or scroll. There are pine trees and purple flowers. Daylight.
why: The mast passes through the man's body, and the sail looks like a block of bricks. There are odd white round pieces floating in the water.

title: Poseidon's Storm
beat: For seventeen days Odysseus steers by the stars until Scheria rises ahead.
text: He sat and guided the raft skilfully by means of the rudder, and never once did sleep fall upon his eyelids as he watched the Pleiads... on the eighteenth day the dim outlines of the mountains on the nearest part of the Phaeacian coast appeared.
guess: Odysseus alone on his raft after leaving Calypso's island, sailing at night/before the storm
sees: Dark night sea of blue studs with wave arches and white foam; a lone figure in red jacket seen from behind standing on a small brown wooden platform; a tall grey sail-like wall behind him; grey rocks in distance.
why: Grey slab (sail?) ambiguous; raft barely visible; figure's face hidden; very dark.

title: Poseidon's Storm
beat: Poseidon sees him, gathers clouds, and strikes the sea with a four-wind storm.
text: He gathered his clouds together, grasped his trident, stirred it round in the sea, and roused the rage of every wind that blows till earth, sea, and sky were hidden in cloud.
guess: A sea god (Poseidon) rising from the waves to confront or raise a storm against a sailor on a raft (Poseidon wrecking Odysseus's raft).
sees: Dark night sea of blue studs with waves; two tall white translucent water spouts/columns; grey rocks. A bearded figure in teal with a gold crown and long white beard rises from the water holding a scepter/trident-like rod. On the right, a man in red at a mast with a white sail, seen from behind.
why: The god is small compared to the man, making scale confusing; the water spouts could be storm or whirlpool; the man's face is hidden; boat barely visible.

title: Poseidon's Storm
beat: The raft rolls; Odysseus is swept away and barely regains it.
text: A sea broke over him with such terrific fury that the raft reeled again, and he was carried overboard a long way off. He let go the helm, and the force of the hurricane was so great that it broke the mast half way up.
guess: Charybdis sucking down and spewing up the sea as Odysseus' raft/ship is wrecked; possibly the storm that destroys his ship.
sees: Dark night sky, blue sea. A man in red seen from behind stands in the water with both arms raised. Ahead, two tall towering columns of white foam/water spout upward and a large grey broken hull piece tilts into the air. Dramatic, dangerous mood.
why: The white spouts read as stacked translucent pieces rather than clearly water; the grey slab's identity as hull is uncertain.

title: Poseidon's Storm
beat: Ino gives him an immortal veil and orders him to abandon the raft and swim.
text: Ino... took pity upon him, and rising like a sea-gull from the waves, took her seat upon the raft. 'Take off your clothes, leave your raft, and swim for the Phaeacian coast. Take my veil and put it round your chest.'
guess: Possibly a man on a small raft at sea with a woman (e.g., Odysseus on his raft with a sea goddess like Ino/Leucothea giving him her veil, or Calypso's raft departure). Uncertain.
sees: Night-dark sky, blue studded sea with arched waves and white foam studs. A small brown patch (raft/deck) with a mast and a big white sail. A bearded man in red studded tunic faces a long-haired woman in a purple top across the mast; grey rock in the water behind.
why: The sail blocks the top half of the woman; the raft is tiny and barely distinct from the sea; the woman's position suggests she might be in the water or on the raft; purpose of the interaction unclear.

title: Poseidon's Storm
beat: Athena restrains the winds except the north wind that drives him shoreward.
text: Minerva... stopped all the winds except one, and made them lie quite still; but she roused a good stiff breeze from the North that should lay the waters till Ulysses reached the land.
guess: Odysseus alone after his ship is wrecked by Zeus' thunderbolt, clinging to wreckage at sea.
sees: Open blue sea with waves, a lone man in a red tunic up to his waist in the water, waving one hand. Floating wreckage: a brown plank piece, a broken mast with a white sail, an oar. Grey rocks and white foam in the distance, dusky sky.
why: His gesture could be waving or grabbing; the scale of the sail and rocks is ambiguous.

title: Nausicaa
beat: Odysseus debates whether to clasp Nausicaa's knees or speak from a distance.
text: Then they began to play at ball... and the ball fell into deep water. On this they all shouted, and the noise they made woke Ulysses, who sat up in his bed of leaves and began to wonder what it might all be.
guess: Nausicaa and her maids playing ball by the river, their cries waking the shipwrecked Odysseus.
sees: LEGO riverside meadow with trees and flowers. A bearded man in red studded tunic sits/crouches on the grass; two women in white with blond hair, one with arm raised as if throwing, by the water; a red-and-white object in the air.
why: Ball is a large odd red/white cone shape; man's posture ambiguous; figures cut off at right.

title: Nausicaa
beat: Covering himself with a leafy branch, he emerges like a mountain lion.
text: He crept from under his bush, and broke off a bough covered with thick leaves to hide his nakedness. He looked like some lion of the wilderness that stalks about exulting in his strength.
guess: Odysseus, naked after shipwreck, covering himself with a leafy branch as he approaches Princess Nausicaa.
sees: LEGO meadow by water. Woman in white dress with blond hair in a bun, seen from behind, holding a bowl; facing her a man in red studded tunic partly hidden behind a leafy green branch/bush; red flowers between them.
why: Branch covers much of the man; woman's face hidden; bowl's meaning unclear.

title: Nausicaa
beat: The maids flee, but Athena keeps Nausicaa steady.
text: The girls scampered off all over the shore and the jutting points, but the daughter of Alcinous stood firm, for Minerva put courage into her heart and took away all fear from her.
guess: Odysseus emerging naked from the bushes covering himself with a branch before Nausicaa, while her maidens scatter (Odyssey Book 6).
sees: Green meadow by a river with stones and flowers, trees. At left a bearded man in pink hides behind/holds a large green leafy branch. In the centre a woman in white with hair in a bun faces him. At right several women in white run away, arms raised.
why: The branch looks like a flat green star piece passing in front of him; the fleeing maidens are seen from behind and overlap each other.

title: Nausicaa
beat: Odysseus praises her tactfully, asks for clothing and directions, and avoids touching her.
text: 'O queen,' he said, 'I implore your aid, but tell me, are you a goddess or are you a mortal woman?... I never yet saw any one so beautiful, neither man nor woman.'
guess: Odysseus, naked, covering himself with a leafy branch as he approaches Nausicaa and her maids by the river
sees: Green meadow by blue water with flowers, trees. A bearded man in pink studded tunic holds a large green leafy branch in front of him; a smiling blond woman in white gown with gold trim stands beside him; another blond girl in white at right edge.
why: The man is clothed, so the branch's purpose is less clear; the right figure is cut off; branch looks like a snowflake-shaped part.

title: Nausicaa
beat: Nausicaa answers with courage and assigns the maids to help him.
text: 'Stay where you are, you girls... this man is some poor waif who has lost his way; give him something to eat and drink, and wash him in the stream in some place that is sheltered from the wind.'
guess: Odysseus, shipwrecked and naked, appears to Nausicaa and her maidens on the Phaeacian shore, holding a branch for modesty.
sees: Grassy shore by blue water with trees; a bearded man in pink/red holds a leafy green branch in front of his body; several young women in white face him, some raising arms in surprise, one with blonde hair seen from behind; a large grey ball-like rock by the water.
why: He is clothed rather than naked; the ball could be the ball they were playing with or a rock.

title: The Lotus-Eaters
beat: They land among the Lotus-eaters and send three scouts inland.
text: On the tenth day we reached the land of the Lotus-eaters, who live on a food that comes from a kind of flower. Here we landed... I sent two of my company to see what manner of men the people of the place might be, and they had a third man under them.
guess: Odysseus's crew landing on an island and meeting its people, perhaps the Lotus-eaters welcoming the sailors (or Nausicaa's maidens).
sees: A sunny island with palm trees and green bushes and a red and black ship beached behind. A group of long-haired figures in white, seen from behind, stand in a ring around a few men. The men include a bearded man in pink with a sword, men in white, and a mustached man in a striped shirt standing on a white pedestal.
why: Most faces are turned away. The striped man stands on an odd white pedestal. The mood could be friendly or threatening.

title: The Lotus-Eaters
beat: The inhabitants offer lotus; those who taste it lose all desire for home.
text: They started at once, and went about among the Lotus-eaters, who did them no hurt, but gave them to eat of the lotus.
guess: The Lotus-Eaters offering lotus to Odysseus' men while Odysseus stands ready to drag them back to the ships.
sees: Green grassy island with palm trees and shrubs by the sea. A long-haired woman in white, seen from behind, holds something small and pinkish out to a bearded sailor in a striped shirt; more crewmen stand behind. Two blond heads fill the left foreground. At right, a man in a red tunic by a red boat raises a sword. A translucent blue cup-like object sits in the right foreground. Bright, calm.
why: The offered object is tiny and partly hidden; large out-of-focus heads crowd the left foreground; the blue translucent object is unexplained.

title: The Lotus-Eaters
beat: Those who ate lotus forgot home and wanted to stay.
text: Those of my men who ate of the lotus never wanted to go back, nor bring news; they only wanted to stay and munch lotus with the Lotus-eaters without thinking further of their return.
guess: Odysseus' men among the Lotus-eaters, lingering after eating the lotus.
sees: Green meadow with large green flowers in the foreground; bearded sailors in striped and white shirts sit on low wooden stools; around them stand smiling women and people in white. Bright, relaxed mood.
why: No visible lotus being eaten; seated figures cut off by flowers; could be any friendly islander welcome (e.g. Phaeacians).

title: The Lotus-Eaters
beat: Odysseus drags the weeping men back, binds them under the benches, and orders immediate departure.
text: I forced them back to the ships, though they wept for it, and bound them under the benches in the ship's hold; then I told the rest to take their places and row out to sea at once, lest any more of them should taste the lotus.
guess: Odysseus and his crew leaving (or landing on) an island, e.g. dragging the crew away from the Lotus-eaters or departing Calypso's/Circe's island
sees: Green island with palm trees and plants at the shore of a studded blue sea; a dark and red longship with oars is beached. Several figures: one in pink with brown hair holding a sword stands by the ship, others (grey-haired, bald/tan, bearded man in white) gather, a long-haired figure and a blond head in the foreground, a blue translucent flask on a white pedestal.
why: Crowded foreground heads cut off; oars appear to pass through the ground; ship's direction (arriving vs leaving) unclear; purpose of blue flask unknown.

title: The Blinding
beat: Polyphemus drinks three bowls, promises Nobody the last death as a guest-gift, and collapses.
text: He fell sprawling face upwards on the ground. His great neck hung heavily backwards and a deep sleep took hold upon him.
guess: Odysseus and his men in the Cyclops Polyphemus's cave; likely the moment around blinding him with the sharpened stake (stake prepared/driven near the eye) with the fire burning.
sees: Dark rocky cave built of tan/grey bricks. A large brown brick-built giant with a single white eye (disc with black center) sits/leans back, arms raised. A long brown log/stake with yellow studs lies across the foreground. On the right, minifigs: a warrior in gold crested helmet, a bearded man in red studded tunic, another helmeted figure, partly behind tall yellow and orange flame-like pieces. A brown round object sits on a rock ledge above. Dim, dramatic lighting.
why: The stake lies low and doesn't clearly touch the eye, so it's ambiguous whether the blinding is happening; giant's pose (sitting vs. falling) is uncertain; flames partly block the men; scale between giant and men is hard to judge.

title: The Blinding
beat: Odysseus heats the stake until it glows and the chosen men drive it into the Cyclops's eye.
text: When the wood, green though it was, was about to blaze, I drew it out of the fire glowing with heat, and my men gathered round me.
guess: In the Cyclops's cave, Odysseus and his men hardening/heating the tip of the olive-wood stake in the fire before blinding Polyphemus.
sees: Dim cave interior with tan brick walls, big pale boulders, and orange/yellow translucent flame-like pieces. A smiling bearded man in red studded tunic stands center with hands raised; behind him two warriors in gold crested helmets. A long brown log with a glowing orange tip extends toward the camera through the fire.
why: The log appears to pass through the man's body/arm; flames and translucent pieces clutter the right; the man's cheerful pose doesn't match the tension; no Cyclops visible.

title: The Blinding
beat: They twist it as blood and steam erupt; Polyphemus wakes with a roar and tears it free.
text: We drove the sharp end of the beam into the monster's eye, and bearing upon it with all my weight I kept turning it round and round as though I were boring a hole in a ship's plank with an auger... the eyeball hissed as a smith plunges an axe into cold water.
guess: Odyssey Book 9: Odysseus and his men blinding the Cyclops Polyphemus.
sees: Dark cave interior with tan/brown rock, fire (orange/yellow flames). A huge brown giant lies at right; a long dark stake with a glowing red tip is thrust into its single eye. A man in red polka-dot shirt and other men (one in a helmet) hold the stake.
why: Close framing, overlapping stake and figures; giant's face fragmented; red effect passes through the stake end.

title: The Blinding
beat: Other Cyclopes call from outside, but leave when he says Nobody is killing him.
text: Then he gave a loud cry, so that the rocks resounded, and we fled in terror; he drew the beam from his eye all bespattered with blood, and hurled it from him in a frenzy of rage and pain.
guess: Polyphemus the Cyclops, blinded (red blood at his eye), as Odysseus escapes under the ram out of the cave.
sees: Low angle in a dark cave of brown rock. A huge muscular giant seen from behind with translucent red blobs around its head; a burning flame/torch at left. On the right, a man in red rides or clings to a pale woolly animal, apparently in the air. Night, menacing.
why: The man is on top of rather than under the animal and seems to float; the red transparent pieces are ambiguous (blood or fire); the pale animal is only partly visible at right edge.

title: The Blinding
beat: Polyphemus gropes at the entrance while the men hide among the animals.
text: Polyphemus, groaning and in an agony of pain, felt about with his hands, took the stone from the door of the cave, and sat in the doorway stretching his hands in front of it to catch anyone going out with the sheep.
guess: Odysseus escaping the Cyclops's cave by clinging to the underside of a ram as Polyphemus lets his flock out.
sees: Low-angle view in a cave or rocky canyon with a peach sky: large white goats/rams stand on a grey studded floor; beneath the nearest ram, a bearded man in red is upside down, clinging to its belly. A brown giant's body looms on the left edge; a log lies on the ground; more rams on a raised platform on the right.
why: The man's body intersects the ram's legs/belly awkwardly; the giant is cut off at the left edge; a grey block near the ram's belly is unidentifiable.

title: The Boast
beat: From offshore Odysseus taunts the blinded Cyclops despite his men's pleas.
text: When I had got as far out as my voice would reach, I began to jeer at the Cyclops. 'Cyclops,' said I, 'you should have taken better measure of your man before eating up his comrades in your cave.'
guess: Odysseus escaping the Cyclops Polyphemus: the blinded giant hurls a rock at the ship as Odysseus taunts him.
sees: A black and red ship with a white sail on blue studded water. Men in red vests and striped shirts are rowing. A bearded man in a pink shirt raises one arm and has a bow near him. Grey rocks are in the foreground, and a huge tan muscular arm or shoulder with a brown strap holds a large white boulder in the lower right. There are trees at the right edge and a pale sky.
why: The giant is only a close cropped shoulder and hand, so scale is hard to read. There is a small red translucent piece near the boulder.

title: The Boast
beat: Polyphemus tears off a mountain peak and hurls it, driving a wave that nearly beaches the ship again.
text: He got more and more furious as he heard me, so he tore the top from off a high mountain, and flung it just in front of my ship.
guess: The Cyclops Polyphemus hurling a boulder at Odysseus (after being blinded) or a giant attacking the hero
sees: A huge muscular brown giant with a red eye area lifting a massive grey boulder over his head amid grey mountains and a pine; a young man in pink with a sword on his back drawing a bow in the foreground right; hazy sky.
why: Boulder hides giant's head/face; the red object (eye? wound?) ambiguous; no ship or sea shown.

title: The Boast
beat: Odysseus rows farther out, then reveals his true name and lineage.
text: The men begged and prayed of me to hold my tongue... 'Cyclops, if any one asks you who it was that put your eye out, say it was the valiant warrior Ulysses, son of Laertes, who lives in Ithaca.'
guess: Possibly Odysseus taunting the Cyclops as they row away, or cheering as they set sail.
sees: LEGO red ship with oars on blue waves, white sail. Bearded man in red studded tunic raising a hand and holding a bow; crewman in red vest with hands up; others behind with hands raised.
why: No other party visible; gesture meaning unclear; figures cropped at top.

title: The Boast
beat: Polyphemus recalls a prophecy, calls on Poseidon, and asks that Odysseus return late, alone, and in pain.
text: He prayed, lifting up his hands to the firmament of heaven: 'Hear me, great Neptune... grant that Ulysses may never reach his home alive; or if he must get back, may he do so late and in sore plight after losing all his men.'
guess: Blinding of the Cyclops Polyphemus with the burning stake
sees: Low angle, dark blue night sky, grey rocky cliff with green plants, a pine. A huge bare-chested tan creature with one large white eye; red translucent flame-like pieces burst at the eye. A sword blade and a bow tip poke in from the left edge.
why: Attacker is off-frame (only sword/bow visible); the giant's head is tiny/oddly shaped; red pieces could be fire or blood; it's outdoors rather than in a cave.

title: The Boast
beat: A second rock misses as the ship escapes to the fleet.
text: He caught up a rock much larger than the first, swung it aloft and hurled it with prodigious force. It fell just short of the ship... the wave it raised carried us onward to the island where we had left the rest of our ships.
guess: Odyssey Book 9: the blinded Cyclops Polyphemus hurling a boulder at Odysseus' departing ship.
sees: Overhead view of a LEGO ship with white sail and oars on blue sea, crew aboard including a man in pink with a bow; a large tan/brown giant figure in the foreground at a rocky shore, with a white round object (boulder) and a spray/splash column rising beside the ship.
why: Giant seen only from behind/cut off; the rock and splash overlap the ship so it looks like it passes through it; scale is confusing.

title: Aeolus and the Bag of Winds
beat: Aeolus hosts Odysseus for a month and listens to the story of Troy.
text: Aeolus entertained me for a whole month, asking me questions all the time about Troy, the Argive fleet, and the return of the Achaeans. I told him exactly how everything had happened.
guess: Odysseus meeting a divine or royal elder on an island, perhaps King Aeolus on his floating island (or Poseidon).
sees: Small grassy island ringed by sand in blue sea with a pine and round tree. An old white-bearded king in white with a gold crown stands left, hands open. A young man in red holds a sword aloft and a bow with arrow. A wave curls in the foreground. Bright day.
why: The bow appears to cross through the man's body and the sword and bow are held at once; it is not clear whether the meeting is friendly or hostile; the old man is not clearly identifiable.

title: Aeolus and the Bag of Winds
beat: He gives a sealed oxhide bag containing every adverse wind and releases the west wind for Ithaca.
text: He flayed me a prime ox to hold the ways of the roaring winds, which he shut up in the hide as in a sack... and bound the mouth of the sack with a silver thread.
guess: Odysseus meeting Athena (in disguise) on the shore of Ithaca after landing, or a castaway supplicating a ruler/deity.
sees: Small island with green grass, sand edge, a round tree and a tall conifer, boulders, surrounded by blue sea with waves; a boat with oars at right. A figure in white with pink cape wears a golden crown-like crest and a bronze helmet/owl-like mask covering the face; a bearded man in pink stands facing them with hands raised.
why: The helmeted figure's face is covered and the helmet overlaps the crown oddly; identity of that figure is unclear.

title: Aeolus and the Bag of Winds
beat: After nine days Ithaca appears, but Odysseus falls asleep at the helm.
text: On the tenth day our native land showed on the horizon. We got so close in that we could see the stubble fires burning... and I, being then dead beat, fell into a light sleep, for I had never let the rudder out of my own hands.
guess: Odysseus sailing home with Aeolus' bag of winds tied up aboard (just before the crew opens it)
sees: LEGO-style longship with dark hull, red side, oars, white sail and brown mast on a studded blue sea at dusk (purple-orange sky). A figure in pink/red tunic with brown hair sits at the stern-ish area, back to viewer. On deck: a tied beige sack, a grey pot/jar, a green bush/plant. Distant white studs in the water, a few wind streaks.
why: No crew visible despite oars; the sack could be any cargo; the tree on deck is odd; figure seen from behind.

title: Aeolus and the Bag of Winds
beat: The crew opens the bag, believing it contains treasure, and the winds blast them back to Aeolia.
text: They loosed the sack, whereon the wind flew howling forth and raised a storm that carried us weeping out to sea and away from our own country.
guess: Odysseus's ship/raft being wrecked by a storm sent by Poseidon (or Zeus).
sees: Night storm at sea: a dark boat hull with red side, a broken mast with torn grey sail, oars, and towering columns of white translucent spray/water crashing over it. A man in red with gold helmet raises both arms on deck; a rock/sack beside him. Small island with trees and boulders to the right.
why: White spray is made of floating translucent pieces that look like clutter; the brown lump next to the man is unidentifiable; the man is seen from behind; boat vs raft unclear.

title: Aeolus and the Bag of Winds
beat: Aeolus refuses further aid, judging Odysseus hated by the gods.
text: 'Vilest of mankind, get you gone at once out of the island; him whom heaven hates will I in no wise help. Be off, for you come here as one abhorred of heaven.'
guess: A hero confronting an old sea god on an island - likely Menelaus seizing Proteus (or a castaway meeting a sea deity)
sees: Small grassy island with trees and a beach amid blue Lego sea; an old white-bearded man in white with a gold crown raising a hand; a young brown-haired man in pink with a cape arriving from the waves at right, reaching out; a boulder behind; calm daylight.
why: Tree between them obscures interaction; scale of young man vs. waves odd; unclear if the old man is a god or king.

title: The Laestrygonians
beat: The fleet enters a narrow harbor ringed by cliffs; Odysseus alone moors outside.
text: We found a fine harbour, with high rocks all round it, and a narrow mouth at the entrance. The captains took all their ships inside... but I kept my own ship outside, and moored it to a rock at the very end of the point.
guess: Odysseus's ship passing through the strait between Scylla and Charybdis (possibly the Clashing Rocks).
sees: LEGO ship with red hull, dark deck, oars and multiple masts with white sail rolls, sailing on blue water between two tall grey rocky cliffs topped with trees. A figure in pink/red with a sword stands at the bow, seen from behind.
why: No monster or whirlpool visible; masts are oddly multiple; hard to tell which rock story it is.

title: The Laestrygonians
beat: Three scouts meet a giant girl who directs them to her parents' house.
text: They found his wife, and she was as big as a mountain; they were horrified at her.
guess: Odysseus' ships trapped in the narrow harbour of the Laestrygonians as a giant attacks (Odyssey book 10); possibly the Cyclops instead.
sees: Brick-built scene seen from the deck of a dark ship with two masts and oars, sailing through a narrow channel between grey jagged cliffs with trees on top. Three figures in white seen from behind on deck. Ahead, a huge tan muscular giant with a red helmet/head and tusked face rises beyond the masts, fists raised. Daylight, blue sky, threatening mood.
why: The giant is half hidden behind the masts and yardarm, so its scale and whether it is in the water or on land are unclear; the red head reads as a helmet or a hood.

title: The Laestrygonians
beat: The queen summons Antiphates, who seizes and eats one scout.
text: Antiphates... raised a cry through the town, which brought thousands of sturdy Laestrygonians running from every quarter: ogres, not men.
guess: A giant attacking sailors, likely the Laestrygonians or the Cyclops attacking Odysseus's men (the men scattering from the giant).
sees: Worm's-eye view against a dusk sky: a huge brown brick giant with raised fists and a grey helmet-like brow looms center; two sailors (a mustached one in striped shirt and a smiling one in red vest with crossed straps) fall or leap in the foreground; a tiny third sailor stands on the giant's head. A brown club/log in the foreground.
why: The man standing on the giant's head is odd; scale is inconsistent; the foreground men appear to float; the giant's face (one eye?) is not clearly shown; it's unclear whether the men are attacking or fleeing.

title: The Laestrygonians
beat: Laestrygonians mass on the cliffs, spear crews like fish, and crush the trapped ships with boulders.
text: They threw vast rocks at us from the cliffs as though they had been mere stones, and I heard the horrid sound of the ships crunching up against one another, and the death cries of my men.
guess: The Laestrygonians smashing Odysseus's fleet with boulders in their harbour (possibly the Cyclops throwing rocks).
sees: A dramatic low angle at sunset. Giant helmeted figures, one tan and one green, stand on grey jagged cliffs lifting and throwing big grey boulders. White splash columns rise from the water. The edge of a red and black ship is at the right, with a tree on the cliff.
why: The extreme angle, floating boulders and splash columns make the scene cluttered. There are cut-off objects in the corners and the scale is confusing.

title: The Laestrygonians
beat: Odysseus cuts his cable and escapes with only his own ship.
text: I drew my sword, and cut the cable of my own ship, telling my men to row with all their might if they too would not fare like the rest... we fell to our oars with a will, and got out into the open sea.
guess: The Laestrygonians attacking Odysseus's fleet with boulders in their harbour (Odyssey Book 10).
sees: Dusk sky; a ship with a mast and crossbar with white cylinders, oars; a bearded man in pink holds up a sword on deck. On grey rocky cliffs either side stand giant muscular figures (trolls/ogres) with helmets, one holding a boulder, and white spray columns rising from the water.
why: Giants partly hidden behind rocks and a tree; one small green figure among them is unexplained; splashes look like floating pieces.

title: Circe Transforms The Crew
beat: The scouts find Circe singing at her loom while enchanted wolves and lions fawn around them.
text: There were wild mountain wolves and lions prowling all round it, poor bewitched creatures whom she had tamed by her enchantments. They did not attack my men, but wagged their great tails, fawned upon them, and rubbed their noses lovingly against them... they could hear Circe within, singing most beautifully as she worked at her loom.
guess: Odysseus' men arriving at Circe's palace, greeted by tame lions and wolves as she offers them her drugged drink.
sees: White columned palace with arches. Inside, a grey-haired woman in purple at a striped loom, with cups/jars on a table before her. A group of men in white seen from behind face her. In front are two golden lions and a grey wolf/dog between stone pillars. Trees outside, bright.
why: The woman looks older than expected; the animals are small and somewhat cartoonish; foreground pillars partly block the view.

title: Circe Transforms The Crew
beat: All but Eurylochus enter; Circe serves drugged food and strikes them with her wand.
text: She set them upon benches and seats and mixed them a mess with cheese, honey, meal, and Pramnian wine, but she drugged it with wicked poisons... and when they had drunk she turned them into pigs by a stroke of her wand. (Eurylochus stayed outside, for he suspected mischief.)
guess: Circe strikes Odysseus' men with her wand after they drink her potion, about to turn them into pigs.
sees: Palace hall with columns, a colourful striped tapestry/hanging, table with jugs. A grey-haired woman in pink raises a wand or staff; men in white hold up cups before her, kneeling or seated.
why: Wand top cut off; the men are seen from behind; the tapestry could suggest Penelope's weaving instead.

title: Circe Transforms The Crew
beat: The men become pigs in body while retaining human minds.
text: They were like pigs, head, hair, and all, and they grunted just as pigs do; but their senses were the same as before, and they remembered everything.
guess: Circe turns Odysseus' men into swine after they drink her potion.
sees: Bright palace room with columns and arched windows; a man in striped shirt wears a pig-head mask/hood and raises his hands in alarm; pink pigs beside him and another pig-headed figure behind; a grey-haired woman in purple holds a goblet at left.
why: The half-man half-pig costume is a bit comical; background cluttered with furniture; woman partly cut off by column.

title: Circe Transforms The Crew
beat: Circe shuts them in pens and throws them acorns.
text: Thus then were they shut up squealing, and Circe threw them some acorns and beech masts such as pigs eat.
guess: Circe penning Odysseus' transformed men as swine and flinging them acorns and cornel fruit.
sees: Garden outside a columned palace; a grey-haired woman in pink stands raising a hand; in the foreground pink pig backs crowd into a brown-fenced sty; round tan acorn/food pieces fly toward them.
why: Pigs seen only as backs, heavy foreground; flying food pieces look like odd discs.

title: Circe Transforms The Crew
beat: Eurylochus runs back to the ship and reports the disappearance.
text: Eurylochus at once came back to tell me about the sad fate of our comrades. He was so overcome with dismay that he could not speak a word; his eyes filled with tears and he could only sob and sigh.
guess: Possibly Odysseus arriving at Circe's palace, surrounded by tame lions (or a return home with a dog). Leaning Circe.
sees: LEGO palace with white arches and tan walls at dusk, stone lion/beast-head statues on pillars, green bushes. Long-haired bearded man in red vest walks forward holding something; a yellow lion-like animal stands in the doorway; grey-haired woman in pink/purple inside.
why: The animal's identity (lion vs dog) is unclear; man walks toward camera away from the building, so direction of arrival is ambiguous; woman small in background.

title: Hermes and the Moly
beat: Odysseus arms himself and heads alone toward Circe's house despite Eurylochus's protest.
text: I slung my bronze sword over my shoulder, took my bow, and told Eurylochus to come back with me... but he laid hold of me with both his hands and spoke piteously.
guess: A hero setting out through a wood - e.g., Odysseus going alone to Circe's house to rescue his men.
sees: A man in pink with brown hair and a sword seen from behind walking along a white stone path through a green forest of conifers, red roses and plants in foreground, a grey rock ahead. Bright calm day.
why: Face hidden; no destination or antagonist visible; could be any journey.

title: Hermes and the Moly
beat: Hermes meets him in the form of a young man and explains Circe's trap.
text: As I was going through the sacred valley, on my way to Circe's house, I met Mercury with his golden wand, disguised as a young man in the hey-day of his youth and beauty.
guess: Odysseus meeting the goddess Athena (in disguise or revealed) who advises him
sees: Forest glade with pines and big leaves, pale path. A man in pink tunic/cape seen from behind reaches toward a smiling figure in a gold crested helmet and white/gold armour who holds a golden staff.
why: Unclear whether hands are exchanging an object; helmeted figure's gender/identity inferred from costume; man's face hidden.

title: Hermes and the Moly
beat: He pulls the black-rooted, white-flowered moly from the earth and gives it to Odysseus.
text: Mercury pulled the herb out of the ground and shewed me what it was like. The root was black, while the flower was as white as milk; the gods call it Moly.
guess: Odysseus conferring with Athena, who carries her spear (or a confrontation with an armed stranger)
sees: Same kind of forest glade. A bearded man in red tunic faces a figure in a gold helmet and white armour with red cape who holds a long black spear/club pointed upward; another black cylinder floats at the top of frame. Grey rock/bowl at right.
why: A black object floats unattached at top; the spear passes through/behind the helmet; gesture ambiguous between argument and conversation.

title: Hermes and the Moly
beat: Hermes instructs him to resist the drug, draw his sword, and force Circe to swear an oath.
text: 'When Circe strikes you with her wand, draw your sword and spring upon her as though you were going to kill her... make her swear a solemn oath by the blessed gods that she will plot no further mischief against you.'
guess: Athena (in helmet) meeting Odysseus on Ithaca and guiding him after his return.
sees: Forest clearing with pines and a pale path. A figure in white armour with a gold crested helmet, smiling, clasps hands with a man in red seen from behind. Bright, friendly.
why: The man's face is hidden; the helmeted figure's identity/gender is ambiguous; big leaves crowd the foreground.

title: The Underworld
beat: The ship reaches the misty land of the Cimmerians at Ocean's edge.
text: She came to the deep waters of the river Oceanus, where lie the land and city of the Cimmerians who live enshrouded in mist and darkness which the rays of the sun never pierce.
guess: Odyssey Book 11, the Nekyia: Odysseus and his crew at the edge of the underworld as the ghosts of the dead gather.
sees: LEGO night scene on grey baseplate with dark pine trees, grey boulders, a ship mast in the background. A group of minifigure men (one in pink/red polka-dot shirt with a bow and sword) stands in the middle. Four translucent white ghost-like figures with stern faces stand in the foreground. Dark, eerie, dim light with a pink glow.
why: Ghosts are in the foreground with backs partly to the camera, faces shown toward viewer so direction is ambiguous; no visible sacrifice or pit; living figures small and clustered behind boulders.

title: The Underworld
beat: Odysseus digs a trench, pours libations, sacrifices sheep, and holds the spirits back with his sword.
text: I dug the trench a cubit each way, and made a drink-offering to all the dead... when I had prayed sufficiently to the dead, I cut the throats of the two sheep and let the blood run into the trench.
guess: Odyssey Book 11: Odysseus sacrifices black sheep at the entrance of the underworld and holds off the ghosts with his sword.
sees: Dark night scene with grey rocks and dark trees. A man in red with a staff raises a sword; men around him, black sheep/rams on the ground, pale translucent ghost figures in the background. Pinkish light.
why: Sheep are dark and hard to read against the dark background; leader's face hidden; ghosts faint.

title: The Underworld
beat: The dead gather in multitudes, crying around the blood.
text: The ghosts came trooping up from Erebus: brides, young bachelors, old men worn out with toil, maids who had been crossed in love, and brave men who had been killed in battle... they came from every quarter and flitted round the trench with a strange kind of screaming sound that made me turn pale with fear.
guess: Odysseus in the Underworld holding off the shades of the dead with his sword (Nekyia)
sees: Dark black setting on grey studs; a man in dark red tunic with brown hair, back to viewer, holds up a sword and a staff. Surrounding him are many translucent pale ghostly figures with smiling faces, one floating higher.
why: Ghosts are generic with cheerful faces; no sacrificial pit visible; hero's face hidden.

title: The Underworld
beat: Odysseus waits for Tiresias before allowing any other shade to drink.
text: I drew my sword and sat there, and would not let the poor feckless ghosts come near the blood till Teiresias should have answered my questions... then came the ghost of the Theban prophet Teiresias with his golden sceptre in his hand.
guess: Odysseus in the Underworld (Nekyia), holding off the shades with his sword at the blood offering.
sees: Dark night scene on grey ground with pine trees and a mast behind; many translucent white ghostly figures with frowning pale heads surround a bearded man in red holding up a sword; companions and dark jars/pits nearby; a golden torch or staff.
why: Many overlapping translucent ghosts obscure the main figures; the golden object is ambiguous.

title: The Sirens' Song
beat: The wind dies as the ship approaches the Sirens' island.
guess: Odysseus's ship passing the Sirens' island, with the Sirens (surrounded by bones) luring the sailors; Odysseus by the mast.
sees: A red ship with a dark deck, mast with a crossbar and white cloud-like piece, and oars in blue studded water. On deck: grey-haired and blond men in white, a bearded man in red at the mast, and a bearded sailor in striped shirt at the stern. On the left shore: a rocky, grassy island with red flowers, white bones, and several long-haired women in white, one on the rock raising a white object (knife or bone), others reaching toward the ship.
why: Odysseus isn't visibly bound to the mast; the sailors reaching out rather than rowing/with plugged ears is ambiguous; the white objects held by women could be bones or blades.

title: The Sirens' Song
beat: Odysseus softens wax and seals every crewman's ears.
guess: Odyssey Book 12: the ship sailing past the Sirens, their meadow full of bones, with Odysseus held/bound.
sees: LEGO shore with green meadow, red and yellow flowers, bones and a skeleton; several long-haired women in teal/white holding wands or flutes, singing. Ship at right with crew; a bearded man in pink polka-dot shirt held among the crew.
why: Ropes/mast binding not clearly shown; figures crowded on the ship; Sirens look like ordinary women.

title: The Sirens' Song
beat: The men bind him upright to the mast and row past the flowering island.
guess: Odyssey Book 12: Odysseus being bound to the mast so he can hear the Sirens.
sees: Close shot of a bearded man in a red/pink polka-dot shirt standing against a ship's mast with white ropes around his chest and legs. Crewmen around him (backs to camera) hold/bind him. Blue sea with waves, clear sky.
why: Foreground crew heads block much of the view; no Sirens visible; man smiling calmly.

title: The Sirens' Song
beat: The Sirens promise total knowledge; Odysseus struggles and signals to be freed.
guess: Nausicaa and her handmaidens playing ball on the shore by the washing place, just before the ball goes astray and wakes Odysseus
sees: Two long-haired young women in white/light-blue dresses on grass near the shore, red and yellow flowers, a white skeletal frame-like object behind; one woman raises a hand holding a white ball; sunny, cheerful.
why: White ribbed object in middle is hard to identify (washing rack? cart? skeleton?); close crop; no third party visible.

title: The Sirens' Song
beat: Perimedes and Eurylochus tighten the ropes until the song fades.
text: Perimedes and Eurylochus bound me with still stronger bonds, till we had got out of hearing of the Sirens' voices.
guess: Odysseus tied to the mast sailing past the Sirens while his crew row with ears stopped.
sees: LEGO ship with mast on blue sea from above; a man in red tied to the mast with white ropes; crewmen rowing; on a green island to the left a blond woman figure with a white object (instrument?).
why: Only one siren partly visible at edge; earplugs not visible; mast hides the bound man.

title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
beat: The crew hears Charybdis roar and sees spray rising from the whirlpool.
text: As she vomited it up, it was like the water in a caldron when it is boiling over upon a great fire, and the spray reached the top of the rocks on either side.
guess: Odysseus' ship passes between Scylla (cave in the cliff) and Charybdis (whirlpool).
sees: Black ship with mast, crewmen at oars, a leader in red at stern, beside a grey cliff with a dark cave containing skeleton bones. On the right a huge white/transparent column of water spouts up from a swirling spot in the sea near rocks.
why: Scylla herself is not visible, only a cave with bones; the waterspout reads more like a geyser than a whirlpool.

title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
beat: Odysseus keeps Scylla secret and orders the men to row hard along her cliff.
text: 'Keep the ship well away from the smoke and surf, and hug the rock, or she will give you the slip.' ... but I said nothing about the awful monster Scylla, for I knew the men would not go on rowing if I did.
guess: Possibly Odysseus's ship passing Scylla's cliff, with the leader arming himself against the monster in the cave.
sees: Close view of a black and red ship crowded with men in white seen from behind. Some raise their hands and one has grey hair. A man in red at the prow holds a sword up and a bow. Oars are in the water. Grey cliffs rise ahead, with a dark opening and small white claw or hand-like objects above.
why: Faces are mostly turned away. The white objects in the cliff opening are small and ambiguous. The leader's figure seems to float beside the hull, and the figures overlap.

title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
beat: He arms himself despite Circe's warning and searches the rock face.
text: I put on my armour and took a spear in either hand, and went on to the fore part of the ship... I strained my eyes with looking the dark rock all over, but I could not see her.
guess: Odysseus and his crew at sea on their voyage home (possibly setting out or approaching a danger).
sees: Top-down view of a black ship with red hull on blue studded sea with stylised wave pieces. A bearded man in red stands at the prow holding a sword and a bow; two curly-haired sailors in white stand near a large brown mast; oars stick out. Island greenery at left edge.
why: No distinct event; the mast dominates the foreground; crewmen partly cut off; nothing indicates which episode.

title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
beat: Scylla's six heads strike, lifting six screaming men from the ship.
text: While we were taken up with this, and were expecting each moment to be our last, Scylla pounced down suddenly upon us and snatched up my six best men.
guess: Scylla seizing six of Odysseus's men as the ship passes her cliff.
sees: A black and red ship by grey cliffs with a dark cave. Many long green coiled necks come from the cliff, ending in green jaws that grip crewmen in white by the head. The men raise their arms. A man in red at the stern aims a bow and holds a sword. Mast and oars.
why: The tangled necks clutter the scene, and the jaws overlap the men's heads.

title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
beat: The survivors pass beyond both monsters while watching their companions die above them.
text: I saw their hands and feet ever so high above me, struggling in the air as Scylla was carrying them off, and I could hear them calling out my name in one last despairing cry.
guess: Scylla seizing six of Odysseus' crew as the ship passes her cliff (Odyssey XII)
sees: Grey rocky cliff with a cave; long dark-green scaly serpent necks emerging from the cave, clutching sailors (blue trousers) lifted into the air; wooden ship mast with crossbar below; a figure in pink with a bow and sword at the mast; overcast sky.
why: Necks pass behind/through sailors and are hard to separate; monster heads not visible; sailors appear upside down and overlap.

title: The Cattle of the Sun
beat: When food is gone, Odysseus withdraws inland to pray and the gods put him to sleep.
text: I went up into the island that I might pray heaven to show me some means of getting away... and when I had washed my hands, the gods sent me off into a sweet sleep.
guess: Odyssey Book 12: landing on Thrinacia with the cattle of Helios (Odysseus warning the crew not to touch them).
sees: Sunny LEGO island, white cattle on the left, crew by a beached red ship behind, trees and water. Bearded man in pink polka-dot shirt in foreground facing the viewer, grinning.
why: No clear action; leader's expression cheerful rather than warning; cattle partly cut off.

title: The Cattle of the Sun
beat: Eurylochus persuades the crew to sacrifice the best cattle rather than starve.
text: 'All deaths are bad enough, but there is none so bad as famine. Why should not we drive in the best of these cows and offer them in sacrifice to the immortal gods?'
guess: Odysseus' crew feasting on Thrinacia beside the cattle of Helios (possibly just a shore feast).
sees: Crewmen in white shirts on a grassy shore holding cups, near a beached red-and-black ship with mast; pine and round trees. At right, large white and brown blocky shapes that look like cattle bodies. A grey pole floats in the air. Daylight, relaxed mood.
why: The white and brown forms at right are cut off and hard to identify as cattle; a grey bar floats in mid-air; nobody is clearly the leader.

title: The Cattle of the Sun
beat: They substitute oak leaves for barley and water for wine, kill the animals, and roast the meat.
text: They drove in the best of the cows... they cut out the thigh bones, wrapped them round in two layers of fat, and set some pieces of raw meat on the top of them. They had no barley, so they strewed oak leaves instead.
guess: Possibly the crew feasting on the island (e.g. slaughtering and roasting Helios' cattle, smoke rising) or the crew celebrating on landing. Uncertain.
sees: Bright daytime LEGO island with green grass, pine tree, grey rock, a ship with mast and red hull behind, water. Several men in white shirts stand around; one in a red vest with long hair raises both hands. A brown object (possibly a roasting pit or carcass/log) in foreground. A translucent white column (smoke) rises in the background.
why: The brown foreground object is hard to identify (roast, carcass, log, rock); no leader clearly shown; cut-off figure at right; smoke column ambiguous.

title: The Cattle of the Sun
beat: The hides crawl and the meat bellows on the spits.
text: The gods now began to show signs and wonders among my men, for the hides of the cattle crawled about, and the joints upon the spits began to low like cows, and the meat, both cooked and raw, kept on making a noise just as cows do.
guess: Odysseus' men slaughtering and sacrificing the cattle of Helios on Thrinacia (smoke of the sacrifice, dead cow).
sees: Five sailors on a green meadow with flowers, all with arms raised, at dusk under a dark red sky. Behind them a beached red-and-black ship with mast and a tall column of white smoke. A brown carcass-like shape lies in the right foreground; a white shape at left.
why: The foreground brown and white forms are cut off and hard to read as carcasses; raised arms could mean joy, prayer, or fear.

title: The Cattle of the Sun
beat: Lampetie tells Helios, who demands punishment from Zeus.
text: 'Father Jove, and all you other blessed gods who live for ever, I must have vengeance on the crew of Ulysses' ship: they have had the insolence to kill my cows... if they do not square accounts with me about my cows, I will go down to Hades and shine there among the dead.'
guess: Odyssey Book 12: the crew on Thrinacia sacrificing/feasting on the cattle of Helios, with the sun god watching (or praying to the gods).
sees: LEGO island at sunset, orange-red sky, a large stylised golden sun with rays, a ship mast, grey rocks, smoke column rising. Five men seen from behind; the middle one raises both arms toward the sun. Trees, flowers, water.
why: No cattle visible; sun is a symbolic giant disc; all faces hidden from behind; could be simple prayer/sacrifice scene.

title: The Wreck
beat: Odysseus wakes, smells the meat, and condemns the act, but the crew feasts for six days.
text: When I had got some way down towards my ship I began to smell hot roast meat, so I groaned out a prayer to the immortal gods... for six days my men kept driving in the best cows and feasting upon them.
guess: Odysseus's ship fleeing a danger such as the Cyclops or the Laestrygonians, with Odysseus ready to shoot (possibly passing the Sirens).
sees: A ship at dusk on blue water. Men with mustaches in white shirts row. At the stern a man in red draws a bow with an arrow nocked and has a sword on his back. There are white sail pieces, translucent ghostly figures and objects, white cones near the rowers, and a grey boulder on the water behind.
why: Several semi-transparent ghostly pieces and figures overlap the crew. The white cones and the target of the arrow are unexplained.

title: The Wreck
beat: On the seventh day the wind falls and the ship leaves Thrinacia.
text: When Jove the son of Saturn had added a seventh day, the fury of the gale abated; we therefore went on board, raised our masts, spread sail, and put out to sea.
guess: Odysseus' ship sailing on, possibly crew stopping their ears as they pass the Sirens or bracing before Scylla.
sees: Dark ship with red hull, mast and white sail on choppy blue sea with white foam. Several crewmen in white row or hold their hands near their faces; a man in red at the stern holds a sword and a bow. A grey rock at back. Daylight.
why: The crewmen's raised hands are ambiguous (cups, rowing, or ears); oars pass through the hull; one head wears an odd green striped piece; leader is not bound to the mast.

title: The Wreck
beat: Zeus gathers a black cloud and strikes the mast with lightning.
text: Jove thundered and hurled a thunderbolt upon the ship, which reeled beneath the blow, and was filled with fire and brimstone.
guess: Odysseus tied to the mast while his wax-eared crew rows past the Sirens
sees: Night; dark ship with tall mast and a white banner/sail; a figure bound high on the mast crossbeam; a group of sailors at the oars with hands raised to their heads; a figure in pink standing apart at right; sea with white foam, rocks.
why: Bound figure is small and obscured by the crossbeam; the separate pink figure confuses who is tied; no Sirens visible; darkness.

title: The Wreck
beat: The ship shatters and every crewman drowns; Odysseus lashes keel and mast together.
text: The men all fell into the sea; they were carried about in the water round the ship, looking like so many sea-gulls... I lashed the mast and keel together, and getting astride of them was carried wherever the winds chose to take me.
guess: The wreck of Odysseus's ship after Zeus's thunderbolt (following the killing of Helios's cattle): his crew drown while he clings to the keel and mast.
sees: Night sea of blue studs with curling dark-blue waves and white foam caps; many minifigs submerged to their heads with hands raised; a bearded man in red sits on a floating brown log/raft; distant island with tree and rocks; translucent spray.
why: White foam caps look like hats and even sit on a head; heads in water read oddly; one drowning figure is smiling; scale of foreground head confusing.

title: The Wreck
beat: Driven back to Charybdis, he hangs from the fig tree until the timbers reemerge, then drifts alone to Calypso.
text: I sprang up to the fig tree, and clung to it like a bat... I clung on till she should spew up my raft again... I let go with my hands and feet, and fell heavily into the sea, hard by my raft.
guess: Odysseus clinging to the fig tree above Charybdis after his raft is sucked into the whirlpool, waiting for the wreckage to be spat back out.
sees: Night scene over blue sea: a tall brown trunk atop a grey rock with a dark green leafy canopy; a bearded man in red studded tunic stands/clings high on the trunk under the canopy. Below, a dark swirling pool with a broken brown log/keel, and grey rocks and foam around.
why: The man seems to stand on the trunk rather than hang from branches; the whirlpool is subtle; small scale in dark scene.

title: Home to Ithaca
beat: Odysseus finishes his tale and the Phaeacians sit in silence.
text: Thus did he speak, and they all held their peace throughout the covered cloister, enthralled by the charm of his story.
guess: Odysseus' ship sailing on/leaving an island; not a specific identifiable episode.
sees: Ship with white sail, red hull, oars, on blue waves at dusk; crew rowing, a man in pink holds a bow; a tree/island behind; white foam at the bottom.
why: No distinctive threat or event; leader's face hidden; foam at bottom ambiguous.

title: Home to Ithaca
beat: Alcinous orders additional gifts packed in a chest and the farewell feast begins.
text: They took the goods they had given him and put them on board the ship; they put the chest of gifts in the ship's hold.
guess: Possibly the crew opening Aeolus's bag of winds (chest) and the storm that follows, or Odysseus threatening mutinous crew.
sees: LEGO red ship on choppy blue sea at dusk with oars, white sail, and a brown chest/box on the mast. Man in red with raised sword and bow; several sailors with hands raised near their heads.
why: Crew gesture ambiguous; the chest's meaning unclear; sword and bow overlap; crowded figures.

title: Home to Ithaca
beat: At sunset Odysseus boards the convoy ship and lies on a prepared bed in the stern.
text: They spread a rug and a linen sheet on the deck at the stern, that he might sleep soundly, and he lay down without a word.
guess: Odysseus asleep on the ship while his crew, near home, gets excited (possibly just before they open the bag of winds); or a sleeping hero carried home by the Phaeacians.
sees: A red boat with a black deck, a mast and white sail, and oars in a blue studded sea with white foam. Five sailors (striped shirts, one with red vest and crossed straps) stand crowded at the stern, arms raised. A person in pink/magenta lies flat on the deck near them. A pine tree appears behind the sail. Dusk purple sky.
why: The lying figure's pose and identity are unclear; sailors' gestures could be celebration or panic; the tree behind the sail is confusing (land or background).

title: Home to Ithaca
beat: The ship runs faster than a hawk while he sleeps and reaches Ithaca before dawn.
text: As four stallions bound together over the plain... even so did her prow curvet as it were the neck of a stallion, and a great wave of dark blue water seethed in her wake. She held steadily on her course, and even a falcon, swiftest of all birds, could not have kept pace with her.
guess: Possibly the ship approaching Scylla and Charybdis (whirlpool at right) or a storm at sea.
sees: Night seascape, LEGO ship with a tattered white sail, red hull, oars, choppy dark blue waves. Four men stand on deck with backs to camera, arms outstretched forward. White spray/whirling column at the right edge.
why: All figures seen from behind; the threat at the right edge is cut off; outstretched arms ambiguous (rowing? reaching? fear?).

title: Home to Ithaca
beat: The crew carries the sleeping man and his treasure onto the shore.
text: They lifted Ulysses with his rug and linen sheet out of the ship, and laid him down upon the sand still fast asleep. Then they took out the presents... and put them all together by the root of the olive tree, away from the road.
guess: Sailors discovering or considering a treasure (e.g., Odysseus's men opening the bag/gifts, or pirates finding buried treasure on an island). Could be the crew eyeing Odysseus's treasure while he sleeps (the magenta figure lying down).
sees: A small island on blue studded water with a big green tree, sand ring, and grey-tan rock. An open brown treasure chest with gold and silver cylinders (coins/goblets) in front. Two sailors seen from behind/side: one in white shirt with grey hair, one bearded in blue-white striped shirt with hand to chin. A pink/magenta object and a gold helmet/head lie near their feet. Dark studded plate in foreground.
why: Foreground dark plate blocks the lower right; the pink/gold object is hard to identify (possibly a lying figure); faces mostly turned away.

title: The Dogs at the Swineherd's Yard
beat: Odysseus approaches Eumaeus's remote pig farm in disguise.
text: Ulysses now left the haven, and took the rough track up through the wooded country... he found Eumaeus sitting in front of his hut, which was by the yard that he had built on a site which could be seen from far.
guess: Odysseus, disguised as a beggar, arriving at the swineherd Eumaeus' hut where the dogs rush him.
sees: Walled farmyard with a thatched hut, trees, a pen of pink pigs at left. An old grey-haired man with a mustache stands by the hut with two dogs. In the foreground a figure in a white hood/cloak seen from behind approaches. Calm daylight.
why: The hooded figure's face is hidden; the dogs look calm rather than attacking.

title: The Dogs at the Swineherd's Yard
beat: Four savage dogs rush him and he drops his staff and sits to avoid attack.
text: The dogs saw Ulysses and flew at him furiously barking; but Ulysses was cunning enough to sit down and loose his hold of the stick that he had in his hand.
guess: An old beggar/herdsman among dogs - possibly the disguised Odysseus arriving at Eumaeus's hut and being set upon by the dogs, or the swineherd calming them.
sees: Close view of four toy dogs (two dark brown, one white, one black) on a tan studded ground, with an old white-bearded man in white with red vest behind, stone wall and a green tree, daylight.
why: Camera very close so dogs dominate and are cut off; dogs are static and do not clearly look aggressive or friendly; the man's role is ambiguous.

title: The Dogs at the Swineherd's Yard
beat: Eumaeus runs out, scatters the dogs with stones, and brings the stranger inside.
text: The swineherd dropped his leather and ran out through the gate of the yard and drove the dogs off by shouting and throwing stones at them.
guess: The swineherd Eumaeus welcoming the disguised Odysseus (as an old beggar) to his hut.
sees: Courtyard of a rustic farmstead with brown fenced hut, tan roof, lamp, grey pots; a brown dog and a white dog; a grey-haired moustached man in white shirt and tan trousers waves; in the foreground an old figure with white hair/beard seen from behind.
why: The foreground figure's face is hidden; the scene's action is mild; dogs static.

title: The Dogs at the Swineherd's Yard
beat: He offers his own seat and prepares two young pigs for a meal.
text: He strewed a bed of brushwood, and spread upon it the skin of a large wild goat... then he went out to the sties where the young pigs were penned, and brought back two of them and sacrificed them.
guess: Odysseus disguised as an old beggar visiting the loyal swineherd Eumaeus in his hut.
sees: LEGO hut interior with wooden walls and tan roof: an old grey-haired man in ragged white/gold clothes standing, an old white-bearded man in red seated on a bench, two pink pigs, and a hearth fire.
why: Which old man is which; pigs overlap each other.

title: The Father Revealed
beat: Athena restores Odysseus's strength, clothing, skin, and dark hair outside the hut.
text: Minerva touched him with her golden wand. First she threw a fair clean shirt and cloak about him; then she made him younger and of more imposing presence; she gave him back his colour, filled out his cheeks, and let his beard become dark again.
guess: No clear event; a hero in armor standing outside a building, perhaps arriving somewhere or an establishing/character shot.
sees: A bearded blond man in white with a dark grey armored breastplate stands alone on tan studded ground; a pale wall behind, a red-orange fluted building/cliff with a doorway at right, clear blue sky.
why: No action, no other characters, no identifying props; figure appears to float slightly above the ground.

title: The Father Revealed
beat: He reenters transformed; Telemachus recoils, believing he is a god.
text: His son was astounded when he saw him, and turned his eyes away for fear he might be looking upon a god. 'Stranger, how suddenly you have changed from what you were a moment or two ago.'
guess: A meeting or greeting between a man and a woman, possibly a reunion (e.g., Odysseus reunited with Penelope, or meeting Nausicaa). Generic encounter.
sees: Sunny outdoor scene on tan studded ground: a woman with blond windswept hair in a blue embroidered bodice raises her hands; facing her, seen from behind, a man with brown hair in white with a pink/magenta cape reaches toward her. A reddish fluted wall/pillar on the left, trees and a low wall in the background, a small orange/grey object behind them.
why: The man's face is hidden; the woman's gesture could be surprise, greeting or fending off; the orange object behind them is unidentifiable.

title: The Father Revealed
beat: Odysseus declares himself the father for whom Telemachus has suffered.
text: 'I am no god,' replied Ulysses; 'why should you take me for one? I am your father, on whose account you grieve and suffer so much at the hands of lawless men.'
guess: A reunion or greeting between two men - possibly Telemachus meeting Odysseus (or a host welcoming a guest).
sees: Two men facing each other near a white railing and a tall brown curtain/wall, with an orange lamp, studded floor, a small conifer in the background. One seen from behind with tousled blonde hair in a blue coat; the other bearded, smiling, in a grey armour-patterned top.
why: Main figure's face is hidden; foreground railing blocks their lower bodies; setting is ambiguous (indoor/outdoor); no distinctive props.

title: The Father Revealed
beat: Telemachus doubts him until Odysseus explains Athena's control of his appearance.
text: 'You are not my father, but some god is flattering me with vain hopes.' Ulysses answered, 'This is Minerva's doing; she does with me whatever she will, for she can do what she pleases.'
guess: A greeting or reunion between the hero and a woman (possibly Odysseus and Penelope, or meeting a woman/goddess on arrival)
sees: Sunny beige studded ground with a brown wall/cliff at left, trees. A woman with wild blond windswept hair in a blue and red embroidered bodice smiles, one hand raised. A man in white with pink cape and brown hair, seen from behind, raises one arm high. Something orange and a grey pedestal behind them.
why: No distinctive props; raised arm could be a wave, a salute or a strike; background object (orange/grey) is unreadable; man's face hidden.

title: The Father Revealed
beat: They embrace and weep with the force of birds robbed of their young.
text: Telemachus threw his arms about his father and wept. They were both so much moved that they cried aloud like eagles or vultures with crooked talons that have been robbed of their half fledged young by peasants.
guess: Odysseus revealing himself to his son Telemachus in Eumaeus's hut, and their tearful embrace.
sees: LEGO interior of a rustic wooden hut with tan roof; two figures embrace tightly, one in white with red cape, one in blue; a fire (orange flame on grey stone) in foreground.
why: Faces largely hidden in the embrace; identity of figures not certain; could be another reunion.

title: Argos
beat: Near the palace Odysseus sees his old dog Argos lying neglected on dung.
text: A dog that had been lying asleep raised his head and pricked up his ears. This was Argos, whom Ulysses had bred before setting out for Troy... he lay neglected on the heaps of mule and cow dung that lay in front of the stable doors.
