guess: Disguised Odysseus and Eumaeus arriving at the palace, where the old dog Argos lies and recognises his master.
sees: LEGO courtyard with tan wall and white arched gateway, trees and flowers, grey path. Two white-haired men in white/gold rags walking toward the gate seen from behind; a brown dog-or-horse-like animal lying by the wall near the gate.
why: Animal looks more like a horse than a dog; faces hidden; scale of animal ambiguous.

title: Argos
beat: Argos lifts his head, drops his ears, and wags his tail at the scent and voice of his master.
text: When he knew Ulysses standing near him he dropped his ears and wagged his tail, but he could not get close up to his master.
guess: Odysseus, disguised as an old beggar, seeing his old dog Argos lying on the dung heap, who recognizes him
sees: Courtyard with white arched gate and beige building. An old man with white hair/beard in white shirt and tan trousers stands at left reaching out; a brown dog stands on top of a large brown pot/mound next to another pot; red object at bottom left.
why: The dog stands atop a pot rather than lying on a dung heap; scale of dog vs pots odd; beggar's face partly hidden by beard.

title: Argos
beat: Odysseus turns aside to hide a tear while asking Eumaeus about the animal.
text: Ulysses looked away and wiped a tear from his eyes without Eumaeus seeing it. Then he said, 'Eumaeus, what a noble hound that is over yonder on the manure heap.'
guess: Disguised Odysseus arriving at his palace with the swineherd Eumaeus and seeing his old dog Argos lying on the dung heap
sees: Courtyard before a cream wall and white arched gate; two old men, one white-bearded in red vest, one moustached in white shirt, greeting; a brown dog standing on a dark brown mound/heap at right; flowers and a tree; bright day.
why: Dog is standing alert rather than lying feeble; which man is the hero is ambiguous; large foreground roses.

title: Argos
beat: After twenty years Argos dies as soon as he has recognized Odysseus.
text: As for Argos, he had hardly seen his master again after twenty years, when the hand of death took him.
guess: Unclear; possibly someone hiding or reaching toward a storage jar outside a palace/house (e.g., a scene at a household courtyard). No confident identification.
sees: Extreme low close-up: a large dark brown round pot/jar with a brown two-tone band in front of a building with a white arch and tan walls; a large black hand (or dark blackened hand/arm) extends horizontally above it. Green lollipop trees and yellow flowers on the left, dusky purple-pink sky, tan studded ground. A small figure in grey is barely visible behind the jar.
why: Camera is too close; the jar dominates the frame; the hand is detached from any visible body and its owner/scale are unknown; the minifig behind is hidden; faces not visible.

title: Eurycleia and the Scar
beat: Penelope orders Eurycleia to wash the stranger's feet because his age resembles Odysseus's.
text: 'Nurse, wash your master's age-mate; I suppose Ulysses' hands and feet are very much the same now as his are, for trouble ages all of us dreadfully fast.'
guess: Probably the foot-washing scene in Odysseus's palace: Eurycleia with the disguised Odysseus while Penelope sits by, perhaps as the nurse turns to tell Penelope.
sees: A columned hall with warm light. An old white-bearded man in a white shirt and dark vest sits beside a grey basin that seems to float. A tall woman in a white gown with a white bun stands facing a dark-haired woman in blue, who seems seated in a dark red chair and reaches out.
why: The basin floats in mid-air and figures are sunk into their chairs. The standing woman's back hides the gesture.

title: Eurycleia and the Scar
beat: Odysseus recognizes the danger but cannot refuse without suspicion.
text: Ulysses was sitting by the fire, but he turned away from the light, for it occurred to him that when the old woman had hold of his leg she would recognise a certain scar which it bore.
guess: The nurse Eurycleia washing the feet of Odysseus disguised as an old beggar, with Penelope nearby, just before she recognises the scar.
sees: A warm-lit hall with white columns. An old white-bearded man in a dark vest sits low. A woman with a white hair bun and white gown holds out a grey basin or tray near him. Behind them is a dark-haired woman in blue. Stud floor.
why: The camera is very low and the studs dominate the foreground. The basin is ambiguous, and it is unclear whether the man is seated.

title: Eurycleia and the Scar
beat: The nurse touches the old boar scar and instantly knows him.
text: She began washing her master, and at once recognised the scar... as soon as she had got the scarred limb in her hands and had well hold of it, she knew it.
guess: Old nurse Eurycleia recognising the disguised Odysseus while washing his feet (basin present), with Penelope/another woman nearby
sees: Columned hall with checkered floor; an old white-haired woman seen from behind embracing or pressed against an old white-bearded man; a basin/dish at his side; a dark-haired woman in blue and brown apron standing nearby holding something white; dim light.
why: Foreground figure's back hides the action; basin and hands overlap; unclear who is embracing whom and what the right woman holds.

title: Eurycleia and the Scar
beat: She drops the foot into the basin, spilling water, and reaches toward Penelope.
text: She dropped the leg, which fell into the bath, making the brass ring and turning it over on its side, so that all the water was spilt on the ground; Euryclea's eyes between her joy and her grief filled with tears.
guess: Eurycleia washing the disguised Odysseus's feet and recognizing his scar, with Penelope present but unaware
sees: Hall with white columns and beige studded floor. An old woman with white bun (seen from behind) holds a basin-like object near an old bearded white-haired man seated; translucent blue water discs at their feet. A dark-haired woman in blue sits nearby at right, smiling.
why: Figures appear embedded in the floor; the basin is oddly placed; Penelope's barrel-like seat blends with her body.

title: Eurycleia and the Scar
beat: Odysseus grips her throat gently but firmly and makes her swear silence.
text: Ulysses caught her by the throat with his right hand and with his left drew her close to him, and said, 'Nurse, do you wish to be the ruin of me?... hold your tongue, and do not say a word about it to any one else in the house.'
guess: The nurse Eurycleia washing the disguised Odysseus's feet and recognising his scar, with Penelope nearby.
sees: LEGO palace hall with white columns and tan walls. Old white-bearded man seated; old woman with white hair in a bun, seen from behind, bending with a light-blue basin of water; another woman in the background.
why: Basin is small and partially hidden; feet not visible; close cropping.

title: The Bow
beat: Odysseus strings the bow effortlessly, as a musician strings a lyre.
text: Ulysses... strung it without any effort, as a skilled bard strings a new peg of his lyre and makes the twisted gut fast at both ends.
guess: Unclear. Possibly a hero standing over or advancing on a fallen monster or giant, or walking a ship's keel.
sees: A bearded man with a helmet or cap in a red studded tunic holds an upright sword and a bow. He is seen at the far end of a long grey segmented object running from the camera toward him, like a stone ridge, a spine or a huge limb. Tan stud ground and blue sky.
why: The large grey foreground object dominates the frame and cannot be identified. Scale is confusing and there is no other context.

title: The Bow
beat: He plucks the string and it sings like a swallow; Zeus answers with thunder.
text: He took it in his right hand to prove the string, and it sang sweetly under his touch like the twittering of a swallow. The suitors were dismayed, and turned colour as they heard it; at that moment, moreover, Jove thundered loudly as a sign.
guess: Hero confronting or attacking a giant (possibly the Cyclops) from below
sees: Low angle against dark blue sky: a figure in red studded tunic with brown hair holds a large grey club/sword and a golden bow; a grey jagged object (a rock or creature's limb) intrudes at upper right with brown underneath.
why: Weapons overlap and pass through each other; the grey object at right is unidentifiable; no context of the opponent; face obscured.

title: The Bow
beat: Telemachus places sword and spear beside him and moves to his father's side.
text: Then Telemachus girded on his sword, grasped his spear, and stood armed beside his father's seat.
guess: Odysseus's archery test: stringing the bow and shooting through the twelve axe heads, with Athena at his side.
sees: LEGO: woman with windswept blond hair and blue/red bodice holding a spear in foreground; bearded man in red studded tunic behind, holding a bow and arrow up; row of axe heads mounted on brown posts at right; tan baseplate, blue sky.
why: Spear shaft crosses the woman's face and foreground; bow and arrow overlap awkwardly; man's raised grey object unclear.

title: The Bow
beat: Odysseus nocks an arrow and shoots cleanly through all twelve axes.
text: He laid the arrow on the centre-piece of the bow and drew the notch of the arrow and the string toward him... he aimed it, and the arrow went right through all the axes, from the first onwards till it had gone clean through them.
guess: Odysseus shooting an arrow through the twelve axes in his hall (the contest of the bow)
sees: Bright hall with white columns, beige studded floor, red-trimmed walls. A row of about a dozen silver axe heads mounted on brown posts. In the foreground a figure in pink/red tunic draws a golden bow with an arrow; a second figure (blond, light blue) stands behind him. Other bearded figures stand at the left near a table.
why: The second figure behind the archer overlaps him; a sword sticks up oddly behind his head; onlookers partly cut off at the left.

title: The Bow
beat: He tells Telemachus that the stranger has not disgraced the house and signals the next phase.
text: 'Telemachus, the stranger within your house has not disgraced you. I did not miss what I aimed at... Now, however, it is time for the Achaeans to prepare supper while there is still daylight.' As he spoke he made a sign with his eyebrows.
guess: Odyssey Book 21: the contest of the bow in Odysseus' hall (stringing the bow and shooting through the axes), possibly Odysseus with Telemachus or a suitor.
sees: Hall with white columns, tables with cups, feasters in background. A bearded man in pink holding a sword and bow faces a younger man in blue; between them a post with axe-heads.
why: Bow and sword overlap the axe-post so things pass through each other; the second man's identity is unclear; the axes are a single post rather than a row.

title: Antinous Falls
beat: Odysseus strips off his rags, leaps onto the threshold, and pours the remaining arrows before him.
text: Then Ulysses tore off his rags, and sprang on to the broad pavement with his bow and his quiver full of arrows. He shed the arrows on to the ground at his feet.
guess: Possibly Odysseus with Athena (spear-bearing goddess) preparing for a confrontation, e.g. before the contest or fight with the suitors; uncertain.
sees: LEGO scene under blue sky on tan baseplate. Woman with wild windswept blond hair in blue/red bodice holding a grey spear; bearded man in red studded tunic raising a grey club/hammer-like object in one hand, holding a bow and a wrapped brown parcel. White pillar at left edge, row of grey cylinders (logs/pipes) in foreground.
why: Parcel and grey cylinders are unexplained; the raised object's identity unclear; no clear action or setting cue.

title: Antinous Falls
beat: He shoots Antinous through the throat while the suitor lifts a cup.
text: Antinous was about to take up a two-handled gold cup to drink his wine... Ulysses aimed an arrow at him and struck him in the throat, and the point went clean through his neck.
guess: Probably a feast in a Greek palace hall, perhaps the suitors feasting in Odysseus's house before the bow contest. The golden curve at the right may be the great bow.
sees: Bright courtyard or hall with white columns, cream walls with red trim, blue sky. Brown tables hold coloured jars and cups. A curly-haired figure in a teal patterned tunic raises a silver cup, with a grey ring over their face. A blond figure in red stands at the right table. A green arm reaches in from behind a column. A large golden curved pole or bow cuts across the right edge.
why: The grey ring covers the main figure's face. Columns block parts of the scene. The golden object at the right edge is cut off and hard to identify. A disembodied green arm pokes out from behind a column.

title: Antinous Falls
beat: Antinous falls across the table, spilling food and wine as the room erupts.
text: He fell over and the cup dropped from his hand, while a thick stream of blood gushed from his nostrils. He kicked the table from him and upset the things on it, so that the bread and roasted meat were all soiled as they fell over on to the ground.
guess: A suitor being struck down at the feast (e.g., Antinous shot through the throat while drinking, spilling his wine) during the slaughter of the suitors.
sees: Close, cluttered interior: a brown table with cylinder cups (white, yellow, orange), red translucent cups/goblets spilling, many red translucent discs on the floor. Behind it a moustached man with long hair in a green and pink ornate shirt leans back with arms flung out. White cloth/curtain and bedpost at left.
why: Very cluttered and close; the man's body is mostly hidden by the table; red translucent pieces overlap each other and pass through objects; no attacker visible.

title: Antinous Falls
beat: The suitors assume an accident and search for weapons that are no longer there.
text: The suitors were in an uproar when they saw that a man had been hit; they sprang in dismay one and all of them from their seats and looked everywhere towards the walls, but there was neither shield nor spear.
guess: Feasting/revelry in a royal hall with the ruler absent - likely Penelope's suitors carousing in Odysseus' palace
sees: Lego Greek-style hall with white columns, checkered tan floor, red-trimmed walls; an empty gold-and-red throne at the back; brown benches holding cups/goblets; several minifigures (purple, red, teal, blue, green) around the edges gesturing; bright daylight, festive mood.
why: Foreground columns block view; figures cut off at edges; faces partly hidden; no clear focal action.

title: Antinous Falls
beat: Odysseus names himself and accuses them of consuming his house and violating his servants.
text: 'Dogs, did you think that I should not come back from Troy? You have wasted my substance, have forced my women servants to lie with you, and have wooed my wife while I was still living.'
guess: Possibly a hero and woman preparing for a contest or battle, e.g. Odysseus with his bow (bow contest / slaying the suitors) with a companion; not a specific identifiable moment.
sees: Two minifigs on tan studded ground against a pale blue sky: left, a smiling woman with windswept blond hair in a blue bodice with red embroidery, holding a grey spear/pike; right, a bearded man in a red studded tunic and brown cap holding a sword in one hand and a bow plus arrows in the other.
why: Plain empty background gives no setting; figures float slightly above ground; no opponent or context; unclear who the woman is or why she holds a spear.

title: The Olive Bed
beat: Penelope orders Eurycleia to move the marriage bed outside the chamber for the stranger.
text: 'Make his bed for him outside the room that he himself built. Bring the bed outside this room, and put bedding upon it with fleeces, good coverlets, and blankets.' She said this in order to try him.
guess: A noblewoman (perhaps Penelope in her chambers with an old nurse such as Eurycleia) greeting or addressing someone in her house at night.
sees: LEGO-style interior at night: tan brick walls, dark doorway, red-roofed area with a dark wooden post, a red/brown table or bed with a gold bar on it, red plates on the floor. A woman minifig with grey-blue hair in a bun, blue top with gold/red chest emblem and white legs raises one hand; behind her a white-haired old woman in white. A yellow hand intrudes from the right edge. Warm lamplight, dim, domestic mood.
why: No clear action; the figure at the right edge is cut off to just a hand; the gold bar on the table is ambiguous (loom? bed?); the older woman is half hidden.

title: The Olive Bed
beat: Odysseus erupts, explaining that he built the bed around a living olive tree and no one could move it intact.
text: 'There was a young olive growing within the precincts of the house... I built my room round this with strong walls of stone... then I cut off the top boughs of the olive tree and left the stump standing. This I dressed roughly from the root upwards and then worked with carpenter's tools well and skilfully.'
guess: A man alone in a house/room at night, perhaps the hero returned home (e.g., Odysseus in his palace) gesturing triumphantly; no clear identifiable event.
sees: Interior corner of a tan-walled room at night (black sky), red roof edge, red and dark red floor plates, a white strip (bed or bench?) on the left. A bearded man in red studded tunic with brown hair raises one fist; a mustard-yellow tile lies in front of him near his feet. Shadowy plant-like shadows on the wall.
why: No other figures; the yellow tile passes through/overlaps his legs; the red floor elements and white strip are ambiguous objects; purpose of gesture unclear.

title: The Olive Bed
beat: The secret proves identity; Penelope runs to him and embraces him.
text: When she heard the sure proofs Ulysses now gave her, she fairly broke down. She flew weeping to his side, flung her arms about his neck, and kissed him.
guess: Odysseus and Penelope embrace after she recognises him, with the old nurse Eurycleia present.
sees: Same kind of tan-brick bedroom with a red-covered bed and tall post, oil lamp on a column. A dark-haired woman in blue and a brown-haired man in crimson embrace tightly; a white-haired old woman in white watches from near the doorway.
why: Faces of the couple mostly hidden in the embrace; the lighting is dim.

title: The Olive Bed
beat: She explains that fear of deception caused her delay.
text: 'Do not be angry with me, Ulysses... I have been shuddering all the time through fear that someone might come here and deceive me with a lying story.'
guess: Penelope and Odysseus reunite in their bedchamber after the test of the bed (bed built around the olive-tree post).
sees: Interior room of tan brick walls with a dark wooden bed with red cover and a tall wooden post; dark doorway. A woman with dark updo in blue dress smiles and faces a brown-haired man in crimson; they clasp hands, standing on a red rug.
why: Man seen from behind, face hidden; could equally be Circe or another hostess; the post could be the olive tree or just a pillar.

title: The Olive Bed
beat: Athena holds back dawn while husband and wife weep and reunite.
text: Minerva... made the night long, and held back Dawn in her golden throne on the Oceanus, nor would she let her yoke her fleet horses Lampus and Phaethon that bear light to men.
guess: Odysseus and Penelope reunited in their bed built around the olive tree trunk, after she has tested him about the bed.
sees: A dim bedroom lit by a single lamp on a gold pole, with warm light and shadows on brick walls. On a raised dark red bed, a woman with a grey bun in blue embraces a brown-haired man in a red robe. A thick wooden post rises from the bed. A dark doorway is at the left.
why: The post could be an ordinary bedpost. The faces are partly hidden.

title: Laertes in the Orchard
beat: Odysseus reaches the farm and finds Laertes alone in patched clothes, tending a tree.
text: He found his father alone, hoeing in a vineyard. He had on a dirty old shirt, patched and very shabby; his legs were bound round with thongs of oxhide to save him from the brambles.
guess: Odysseus finding his father Laertes working in his orchard
sees: Apple orchard on green studs with grey stone wall; a bearded man in pink studded tunic stands smiling; an old white-haired man in tan clothes, seen from behind, holds a long grey tool (hoe/spade) near the trees. Brown garden bed at left.
why: The tool is oversized and angled oddly; old man's face hidden.

title: Laertes in the Orchard
beat: He sends his companions to prepare food and approaches under another false identity.
text: Ulysses stood under a tall pear tree and wept to see him so old and so broken... he made up his mind to go up to him and question him.
guess: Odysseus meeting his old father Laertes working in the orchard.
sees: LEGO orchard on green baseplate with apple trees bearing large red apples, grey stone wall bricks behind. Bearded man in pink/red studded tunic faces an older white-haired figure in gold/tan clothing seen from behind, holding a grey tray/tool with an apple.
why: Old man's face hidden (back view); apples overlap his body; tray/tool object ambiguous.

title: Laertes in the Orchard
beat: He claims to have hosted Odysseus years earlier and watches his father collapse in grief.
text: A dark cloud of sorrow fell upon Laertes as he listened. He filled both hands with the dust from off the ground and poured it over his grey head, groaning heavily as he did so.
guess: Laertes overcome with emotion as Odysseus reveals himself in the orchard
sees: Apple orchard; an old white-haired man in tan clothes kneels or crouches with a hand to his face, a grey tool lying across him. A smiling bearded man in pink tunic stands behind him.
why: The tool floats/passes across the old man's body; the old man's pose (kneeling vs sitting) is awkward; the younger man's cheerful face doesn't match the emotion.

title: Laertes in the Orchard
beat: Unable to continue, Odysseus embraces him and names himself.
text: 'I am he, father, about whom you are asking; I have returned after being away for twenty years.'
guess: Odysseus reveals himself to his aged father Laertes in the orchard and they embrace.
sees: Orchard of dark green trees with large red apples; grey stone wall behind. A brown-haired man in crimson and a white-haired man in brown/tan clothes embrace closely. A grey pole or tool juts in from the right.
why: Very close crop; the figures overlap and faces are partly hidden; the grey pole (digging tool?) intrudes oddly.

title: Laertes in the Orchard
beat: Laertes asks for proof beyond desire.
text: 'I will tell you the trees you gave me in this garden... you gave me thirteen pear trees, ten apple trees, and forty fig trees.' Laertes' strength failed him when he heard the proofs, and he flung his arms about his son.
guess: Odysseus proving his identity to Laertes by naming the fruit trees his father gave him as a boy.
sees: LEGO apple orchard with many trees full of red apples, grey stone wall. Man in pink/red seen from behind pointing up at trees; white-haired old man in gold/tan clothing beside him, hands raised.
why: Both faces mostly hidden; gesture meaning inferred; apples are oversized.

title: Laertes Restored
beat: Laertes is bathed and anointed inside the farmhouse.
text: The Sicel woman bathed Laertes and anointed him with oil, and put a good cloak on him.
guess: A king receiving or judging someone at his palace (possibly King Alcinous welcoming a guest); no specific event evident
sees: Close-up of a bearded, stern man in a gold crown and ornate pink/gold robe, hands resting on a brown bench or table, in front of a cream castle wall on green grass; bright daylight.
why: Only one figure; no context or other characters; the bench seems to pass through his body.

title: Laertes Restored
beat: Athena makes him taller and stronger, restoring royal presence.
text: Minerva came up to him and gave him a more imposing presence, making him taller and stronger than before, and when he came back his son was surprised to see him looking so like an immortal.
guess: A king standing before his palace, perhaps a Greek king receiving a visitor. No specific event can be identified.
sees: A bearded man with a tall gold crown and an ornate pink and gold robe stands facing the viewer on green grass. Behind him is a white building with red crenellations and a brown bench. There is a red canopy edge above and a pale sky.
why: There is no action or other figures. The king is shown alone, so there is no story context.

title: Laertes Restored
beat: Dolius and his sons return from the fields, recognize Odysseus, and join the feast.
text: Dolius came up with both arms outstretched, took Ulysses' hand, and kissed it on the wrist. 'Welcome home,' said he.
guess: Odysseus revealing himself to his father Laertes in the orchard (or the reunion that follows)
sees: Orchard of apple trees on green studded ground with grey stone wall. A figure in a gold crown, pink tunic and purple cape seen from behind faces an old grey-haired man with mustache in tunic and brown trousers who raises both hands. Behind are figures in silver Roman-style helmets and another in pink; a man in brown trousers partly hidden by a tree.
why: Crowned figure's identity unclear (crown suggests a king); helmeted figures cluttered behind; one figure is hidden behind a tree trunk; faces of main figure hidden.

title: Laertes Restored
beat: The reunited household eats while rumors of the massacre spread through town.
text: They took their seats in order on the benches and chairs... and began to eat, while Dolius and his sons did the same.
guess: A king's banquet with warriors - possibly King Alcinous hosting a feast, or a council/feast of kings.
sees: Outdoor feast on green grass: a brown table with round white, yellow and red dishes; seated figures include a grey-haired moustached man, a crowned bearded man in red, two figures in silver Roman-style helmets in red, and a figure in cream with a large headdress. Cream building behind with red top. Bright daylight.
why: Foreground helmet figure blocks the view; the cream figure on the right has an odd oversized headdress; faces of seated figures partly hidden; no single focal action.
